---
title: "Split clips"
description: "Cut clips in two at the playhead, and see what each piece keeps of the footage, actions, word timings and graphics."
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Split cuts a clip in two at the playhead, so you can trim, move or remove one piece without touching the other.

<AtAGlance
  menu="Clip ▸ Split"
  keys="⌘T"
  where="The scissors button in the timeline bar"
  tools="split"
/>

## Split at the playhead

<Steps>

1. Move the playhead to the frame you want to cut on.

2. Select the clips to cut, or select nothing to cut everything under the playhead.

3. Press <kbd>⌘T</kbd>.

</Steps>

| What's selected | What gets cut |
| --- | --- |
| One or more clips | Each selected clip the playhead is inside |
| Nothing | Every clip under the playhead on every unlocked track |

It's one undo step, named Split, however many clips it cuts. The command is available whenever the timeline has clips.

The playhead has to be strictly inside a clip. A playhead sitting exactly on a clip's edge is at a cut already, so that clip is left alone. If nothing can be cut, Frame Job beeps and nothing changes.

A clip on a locked track is left alone when nothing is selected, but it's still cut if you selected it.

## Footage stays continuous

The second piece carries on playing the footage from where the first stopped, at the same speed, so the split doesn't show when you play it back. The second piece starts from the values the clip had reached at the cut, and keeps its name, label and settings.

On a clip with a [speed ramp](/speed/edit-a-ramped-clip/), the two pieces meet at exactly the same point in the footage, and the second starts at the rate in force at the cut.

## Linked sound

A [linked clip](/audio/detach-and-attach/) on an unlocked track is cut too, when the playhead is inside it, and the two second halves are linked to each other.

If the linked clip isn't cut, because its track is locked or the playhead isn't inside it, it stays linked to whichever piece shares more of its time. The other piece isn't linked to anything.

## Actions and word timings

[Actions](/motion/how-edits-move-actions/) stay with the piece they fall in:

- An action that ends at or before the cut stays on the first piece.
- An action that starts at or after the cut moves to the second piece.
- An action that spans the cut becomes two. The first half ends at the value it had reached at the cut, and the second carries on to the original target, so the join doesn't show. Both keep the action's curve.

An [entrance and exit preset](/motion/entrances-and-exits/) is tied to the clip's ends, so the first piece keeps the entrance and the second keeps the exit. A [text reveal](/text-and-shapes/text-reveal/) divides the same way. Otherwise the clip would leave at the cut and arrive again on the far side of it.

Caption word timings stay on their words. Both pieces keep the full text, the first with its timings as they were and the second with its timings moved to match its new start.

The one exception is a text clip whose wording an action changes. If the second piece's text at the cut no longer has the same number of words as its timings, the second piece loses its word timings and shows its text all at once.

## Split a graphic

A [graphic](/graphics/size-and-timing/) carries on across the cut rather than starting again, and plays its outro once, at the true end.

The graphic's **In** on the second piece starts at the cut, so it picks up where the first piece left off. Both pieces keep the original's **Length**, so an outro still plays at the same moment. That pins the length, so **Follow Clip** is off on both pieces afterwards.

Trimming the start of a graphic, or [rolling the cut](/editing/slip-and-roll/#roll-a-cut) before it, moves **In** in the same way. Trimming the end leaves a pinned **Length** alone. With **Follow Clip** on, the graphic's own timeline ends at the new end.

## Good to know

- The cut lands on the project's frame grid.
- A [transition](/motion/transitions/) into the clip stays on the first piece. The second piece starts with a hard cut.
- [Sound fades](/audio/fades/) are copied to both pieces. A clip with a fade-in fades in again at the cut, and one with a fade-out dips at the cut, so set them again on the side of the cut where you don't want them.
- A project holds up to 4,096 clips, and a split that would pass that is stopped with a message at the foot of the inspector.

## Related

- [Split at Shot Changes](/editing/split-at-shot-changes/)
- [Delete, Ripple Delete and Lift](/editing/delete-clips/)
- [Trim clips](/editing/trimming/)
- [How edits move actions](/motion/how-edits-move-actions/)

---
title: "Split at Shot Changes"
description: "Cut a finished edit, a download or a stream recording into one clip per shot, with the cuts found on your Mac."
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Split at Shot Changes takes a clip that already has cuts in it, such as a finished edit, a downloaded clip or a stream recording, and cuts it at each one, giving you one clip per shot.

<AtAGlance
  menu="Clip ▸ Split at Shot Changes"
  tools={['split_at_shots', 'get_media_analysis']}
  needs="Nothing. The cuts are found on your Mac, with no key and no upload."
/>

## Split a clip at its shot changes

<Steps>

1. Select one or more clips that show a video file's picture.

2. Choose **Clip ▸ Split at Shot Changes**. It has no shortcut.

3. If Frame Job hasn't looked at this footage yet, wait for the [Analyzing sheet](#while-the-cuts-are-found) to finish.

</Steps>

Each selected clip is cut at every hard cut inside the part of the file it plays. All the cuts are one undo step, named Split at Shot Changes.

The command is greyed out until a selected clip shows a video file's picture. Anything else in the selection is left alone: text, an image, a freeze frame, an audio file, a nest, or a clip with its [picture turned off](/editing/enable-picture-and-sound/).

If the footage holds no shot change inside any selected clip, Frame Job beeps and nothing changes.

## While the cuts are found

When the footage has already been read, the split lands at once. Otherwise the **Analyzing** sheet appears, with one row per file:

| A file's row reads | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| Waiting | Its first frame hasn't been read yet. |
| A percentage, with a bar | How much has been read. |
| Done | Its cuts have been found. |

The split lands as soon as every file is done. Editing commands are off while the sheet is up.

**Stop** closes the sheet and changes nothing. What Frame Job had already found stays in the cache, so it doesn't start from nothing next time.

If the project changes while the sheet is up, nothing is split, and the inspector says to choose the command again.

## What counts as a hard cut

A hard cut is a change from one picture to another between two frames. Frame Job compares each frame's colours with those of the frames before it. It's a plain measurement of the picture, with no machine learning, so the same footage always gives the same cuts.

- A gradual dissolve isn't a cut.
- A single flash frame isn't a cut, because the picture after it matches the one before.
- A dissolve between flat-coloured pictures, such as slides or title cards, can be found as one cut.
- Two shots with very similar colours can be missed, because the comparison looks at colour rather than at what's in the frame.
- Of two cuts within 12 frames of each other in the file, only the stronger is found.

## Found on this Mac and cached

Shot changes are found on your Mac. Nothing is sent anywhere and you don't need a key.

The results are kept in the project's cache, so a second split of the same footage starts at once. See [On-device media analysis](/projects/media-analysis/).

## Where the cuts land

Each cut lands on the project's frame grid, worked out through the clip's speed, [speed ramp](/speed/speed-ramps/) and [reversal](/speed/reverse/). In a project whose frame rate differs from the file's, that's the nearest project frame.

A cut within one frame of either end of a clip isn't made, so you won't get a piece one frame long at a clip's edge.

Each cut is an ordinary [split](/editing/splitting/), so actions, word timings and graphics divide the same way.

## Locked tracks and linked sound

A selected clip on a locked track is still cut. Its linked sound is cut with it when the sound's track is unlocked, as with [Split](/editing/splitting/#linked-sound).

## The clip ceiling

A project holds up to 4,096 clips, counting the clips inside nests. If the splits would pass that, nothing is split at all, and the inspector says how many clips the command would add and how many more would fit. The count includes each linked clip the splits also cut.

## When it can't run

Frame Job beeps and gives the reason at the foot of the inspector:

| What happened | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| A file is missing or can't be read | [Relink it](/projects/relink-media/), then choose the command again. |
| The analysis of a file failed | The message names the file and the reason. Nothing is split. |
| The analysis is no longer in the project's cache | Choose the command again, and Frame Job reads the file again. |

## With an agent

`split_at_shots` works on the clips it's given. Without a list, it takes every clip of a video file on an unlocked track, so a clip on a locked track is cut only when it's named. It shows no sheet. It waits up to 60 seconds for the cuts, and if they aren't ready it stops without splitting and keeps what was found, so calling it again carries on.

`get_media_analysis` reads a file's cuts without splitting anything. See [Tools: cutting and deleting](/mcp/tools-cut-and-delete/).

## Related

- [Split clips](/editing/splitting/)
- [On-device media analysis](/projects/media-analysis/)
- [Select clips](/timeline/selecting-clips/)

---
title: "Delete, Ripple Delete and Lift"
description: "Remove clips or a stretch of the timeline, and choose whether the hole stays open or closes up."
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

There are two delete keys, and the difference between them is what happens to the hole. <kbd>⌫</kbd> leaves it open, so everything else keeps its timing. <kbd>⌘⌫</kbd> closes it, so the rest of the timeline moves left.

<AtAGlance
  menu={['Edit ▸ Delete', 'Edit ▸ Ripple Delete']}
  keys={['⌫', '⌘⌫']}
  where="The Ripple Delete button in the timeline bar"
  tools={['delete', 'ripple_delete', 'lift_range', 'ripple_delete_range', 'ripple_delete_ranges']}
/>

## Choose a delete

Each key acts on the selection, or on the [in/out range](/timeline/in-out-range/) when nothing is selected.

| | Clips selected | Nothing selected, a range set |
| --- | --- | --- |
| <kbd>⌫</kbd> **Edit ▸ Delete** | **Delete:** removes the clips and leaves gaps. | **Lift:** removes what's in the range and moves nothing. |
| <kbd>⌘⌫</kbd> **Edit ▸ Ripple Delete** | **Ripple Delete:** removes the clips and closes each hole. | **Ripple Delete:** removes what's in the range and closes the hole. |

A selection takes priority over a range, so [deselect](/timeline/selecting-clips/) first to act on the range. An empty range is ignored. With nothing to remove, both menu items are greyed out and the keys beep.

## Delete clips and leave a gap

Select the clips and press <kbd>⌫</kbd>. They go, the gaps stay, and nothing else moves. It's one undo step, named Delete.

- A picture takes its [linked sound](/audio/detach-and-attach/) with it, unless the sound's track is locked.
- A linked sound clip goes alone, and leaves its picture silent.
- A clip on a locked track that you selected by clicking is still removed.

## Ripple delete clips

Select the clips and press <kbd>⌘⌫</kbd>, or use the timeline bar's button. The clips go, and each hole closes: everything later on every unlocked track moves left. It's one undo step, named Ripple Delete.

Set an in/out range, select nothing and press <kbd>⌫</kbd>. Every clip on an unlocked track is cut at both ends of the range, and what lies between is removed. Nothing moves, markers included. It's one undo step, named Lift.

Set an in/out range, select nothing and press <kbd>⌘⌫</kbd>. Every clip on an unlocked track is cut at both ends of the range, what lies between is removed, and the hole closes. It's one undo step, named Ripple Delete.

Each hole closes with one shift of everything after it, so clips that touched before still touch.

3. The selected clips.
4. The in/out range.

While you type in a text field, both menu items are greyed out, so <kbd>⌫</kbd> and <kbd>⌘⌫</kbd> edit the text. That covers the timecode fields, a rename and a text clip.

While a point is selected in a [curve](/color/curves/), <kbd>⌫</kbd> deletes the point and **Edit ▸ Delete** is greyed out.

---
title: "Close gaps and insert time"
description: "Close an empty stretch of a track with a double-click or Close Gap, and open room on the timeline when you need it."
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Closing a gap pulls everything after it back to meet what's before it, on every unlocked track, so the timeline stays in sync. Opening room does the opposite.

<AtAGlance
  menu="Clip ▸ Close Gap"
  where="Double-click an empty stretch of a lane"
  tools={['close_gap', 'insert_time']}
/>

## Double-click a gap

Double-click an empty stretch of a lane. Everything after the gap, on every unlocked track, moves left by the gap's length. It's one undo step, named Close Gap.

This only works on a lane. Above the first lane or below the last, no track is named, so there's nothing to close.

## Close the gap under the playhead

Move the playhead into a gap and choose **Clip ▸ Close Gap**. It has no shortcut.

It works on the current track: the selected clip's track or, with nothing selected, the front track. The result is the same as a double-click. The command is available when the timeline has clips.

## What moves

- A gap is the empty stretch between two clips on that track. A gap before the first clip closes back to the start of the timeline.
- Every clip on an unlocked track that starts at or after the far side of the gap moves left. A clip on another track that spans that point stays where it is.
- A moved clip's [linked partner](/audio/detach-and-attach/) moves too, when its track is unlocked.
- [Markers](/timeline/markers/) don't move.
- A clip that ends up overlapping the one before it, within the [overlap rule](/getting-started/refused-edits/), gets a Cross Dissolve.

## When a gap won't close

A gap closes completely or not at all. Frame Job beeps, moves nothing and gives the reason at the foot of the inspector when:

| What's wrong | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| The point is on a clip, not in a gap | Move the playhead into the gap, or check the current track. |
| No clip follows the gap on that track | There's nothing to pull back. |
| The track is locked | [Unlock it](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/). Its clips are the ones that would stay behind. |
| Closing it would push clips into an overlap the overlap rule forbids, on any track that moves | Trim or move those clips first. |
| A linked clip would go before the start of the timeline | Happens when a sound leads its picture, as in a [J-cut](/audio/j-and-l-cuts/). Move the pair later, or trim the sound. |

## Insert time

Inserting time opens empty room. Every clip on an unlocked track that starts at or after a point moves later by a length, and so does every marker at or after that point, unlike a ripple.

Clips that span the point stay put, so nothing is cut. To open room inside a clip, [split](/editing/splitting/) it first.

Inserting time has no menu item or gesture of its own. An ⌥-drop [insert](/editing/insert-and-overwrite/) and [Freeze Frame](/speed/freeze-frame/) both do it as part of their edit, and an agent can do it directly with `insert_time`. See [Tools: cutting and deleting](/mcp/tools-cut-and-delete/).

## Open room by hand

<Steps>

1. Move the playhead to where the room should start.

2. Press <kbd>⌥⌘A</kbd> (**Edit ▸ Select After Playhead**) to select every clip that starts at or after the playhead.

3. Drag the selected clips later, or press <kbd>⇧.</kbd> to [nudge](/editing/nudge-clips/) them 10 frames at a time.

</Steps>

This differs from inserting time in two ways: it also moves the selected clips on locked tracks, and it leaves markers where they are. Start the drag on a clip on an unlocked track, because a clip on a locked track can't be grabbed.

## Related

- [Delete, Ripple Delete and Lift](/editing/delete-clips/)
- [Insert and overwrite](/editing/insert-and-overwrite/)
- [Nudge clips](/editing/nudge-clips/)
- [Hide and lock tracks](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/)

# CLAUDE.md — the documentation site

The public user documentation: Astro with Starlight, one page per feature or tight family of
features. `pnpm` manages it, Node is pinned by `.node-version`. `README.md` has the commands.

## Where things are

```
astro.config.mjs        Starlight's settings: title, logo, fonts, theme, plugins
sidebar.mjs             every page's place in the navigation, in order
src/content/docs/       the pages: <section>/<page>.mdx
src/data/features.json  THE FEATURE LIST: what /features/ renders and what the proof reads
src/components/         AtAGlance (a page's facts), Shot (a screen in both looks),
                        FeatureIndex (the filterable list)
src/assets/screens/     WebP captures, written only by scripts/import-screens.mjs
src/styles/             the brand: the mark's inks, the app's faces, square chrome
```

## The rule that matters

**Every claim is written from the code.** A label, a default, a range, a shortcut, a limit or a
refusal is checked against `app/Sources/`, `core/src/`, `graphic/` or `mcp-proxy/` before it is
written, and the code wins over `docs/guide/`, a spec or an ADR. Never write what a feature
probably does. If the code cannot settle it, leave it out.

Nothing dev-only, deferred or unbuilt is documented. That excludes the dev tools (`snapshot_ui`,
`perform_menu_item`, `cancel_sheet`, `select_inspector_tab`, `play_preview`, `graphic_memory`,
`loudness_meter`, `land_recording`, `analysis_job`, `transcript_view`, `playback_rebuilds`,
`assistant_send`, `assistant_answer`) and every `-RCDev` launch default.

## Who reads this

Someone editing a video, who has never read this repository. They want to know what a thing does,
how to do it, and what will stop them. They do not care how it is built.

So a page never mentions: spec or decision IDs (`AU-12`, `§11`), road maps, phases, issue numbers,
source file or type names, `rc_*` exports, format version numbers, proofs, tests, or the history
of a feature. Internal words get translated: "refused" becomes what the user sees ("Frame Job
won't do this while…"), "the core" and "the op" disappear. A tool name is the one exception: the
MCP pages and `tools=` in `AtAGlance` name agent tools, because those are the product's interface.

## Voice

- Plain, direct and second person. Say what it does, then how. Short sentences.
- Open with what the feature is for, in a sentence or two, before any steps.
- British spelling in prose, as `docs/guide/` does (colour, centre, grey, normalise), and the
  app's exact spelling for its own labels (the **Color** tab, **Normalize**).
- Contractions are fine. No marketing: never "powerful", "seamless", "effortless", "robust",
  "simply", "just", "easily", "unleash", "supercharge".
- Prefer a full stop or a comma to an em dash.
- State defaults, ranges and limits as numbers. Say what happens at the edges, because that is
  what a reader comes to a reference for.
- No filler sections. A page with nothing to say under a heading doesn't have that heading.

## Page shape

```mdx
---
title: Markers
description: One sentence, what this page helps you do. Search results show it.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

What the feature is for, in a sentence or two.

<AtAGlance menu="Mark ▸ Add Marker" keys="M" tools="add_marker" />

<Shot name="04-editor.window" alt="What the picture shows, for someone who can't see it." />

## Add a marker

<Steps>

1. Move the playhead to the moment.
2. Press <kbd>M</kbd>.

</Steps>

## Options

| Control | What it does | Default |
| ------- | ------------ | ------- |

## Good to know

Limits, edge cases and what stops it, in plain words.

## Related

- [Snapping](/timeline/snapping/)
```

Every section is optional except the opening. Order the task sections as a reader needs them.

- **Headings** start at `##`, are sentence case, and name the job: "Add a marker", not "Adding".
  A feature in `src/data/features.json` with an `anchor` needs a heading that makes that anchor.
- **Menus** are bold with `▸`, spelled as the app spells them: **Clip ▸ Split**.
- **Keys** use the app's symbols in `<kbd>`: <kbd>⌘T</kbd>. Inside `AtAGlance`, pass the string.
- **Controls** are bold where they appear in a step: choose **Save**.
- **Links** are root-absolute with a trailing slash: `/timeline/markers/#add-a-marker`. The build
  fails on a link or anchor that does not exist.
- **Asides** are for what a reader must not miss, not for decoration: `:::note`, `:::tip`,
  `:::caution`, `:::danger`.
- **Screens** come from `src/assets/screens/`. A `name` is the file name without its look and
  extension. Use a screen only when it shows what the page is about, not when the thing is out
  of frame, and give it real alt text.

## MDX traps

MDX is JSX. In prose, `{`, `}` and `<` start code. Put anything like `{x}`, `<1 s` or `a<b` in a
code span, or write it out ("under 1 s"). `<kbd>` and every component must close. A line starting
with `import` or `export` is code. Leave a blank line after an opening component tag and before
its closing tag, or the Markdown inside won't render.

## Checking a page

```sh
node docs/site/scripts/check-pages.mjs <page.mdx>…        # parses, imports, links, captures
python3 tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py --pages <page.mdx>…  # internal words, local paths
pnpm build                                                # in docs/site: the last word
```

## Screens

The captures come from the screen catalog (`designs/screens/`, `tools/proof/screens.py`), so the
pictures are of the real app. To refresh them:

```sh
python3 tools/proof/screens.py --out <dir>                      # from the repository root
node docs/site/scripts/import-screens.mjs <dir> --used
```

**This site is public.** `import-screens.mjs` refuses a capture whose layout dump holds a local
path, and its `CROP` table is the only way past that, by cutting the region away. Settings needs
it: its MCP section prints the helper's full path. Never weaken the refusal.

## When the app changes

A user-visible change edits its page here as well as `docs/guide/`, and a new feature adds its row
to `src/data/features.json`. `tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py` runs in `make test` and fails on a
menu item or agent tool the site doesn't document, a feature whose page or anchor is missing, or a
page that names something internal.

Nothing dev-only, deferred or unbuilt is documented. That excludes the dev tools (`snapshot_ui`,
`perform_menu_item`, `cancel_sheet`, `select_inspector_tab`, `play_preview`, `graphic_memory`,
`loudness_meter`, `land_recording`, `analysis_job`, `transcript_view`, `playback_rebuilds`,
`assistant_send`, `assistant_answer`) and every `-RCDev` launch default.

## Who reads this

Someone editing a video, who has never read this repository. They want to know what a thing does,
how to do it, and what will stop them. They do not care how it is built.

So a page never mentions: spec or decision IDs (`AU-12`, `§11`), road maps, phases, issue numbers,
source file or type names, `rc_*` exports, format version numbers, proofs, tests, or the history
of a feature. Internal words get translated: "refused" becomes what the user sees ("Frame Job
won't do this while…"), "the core" and "the op" disappear. A tool name is the one exception: the
MCP pages and `tools=` in `AtAGlance` name agent tools, because those are the product's interface.

## Voice

- Plain, direct and second person. Say what it does, then how. Short sentences.
- Open with what the feature is for, in a sentence or two, before any steps.
- British spelling in prose, as `docs/guide/` does (colour, centre, grey, normalise), and the
  app's exact spelling for its own labels (the **Color** tab, **Normalize**).
- Contractions are fine. No marketing: never "powerful", "seamless", "effortless", "robust",
  "simply", "just", "easily", "unleash", "supercharge".
- Prefer a full stop or a comma to an em dash.
- State defaults, ranges and limits as numbers. Say what happens at the edges, because that is
  what a reader comes to a reference for.
- No filler sections. A page with nothing to say under a heading doesn't have that heading.

## Page shape

```mdx
---
title: Markers
description: One sentence, what this page helps you do. Search results show it.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

What the feature is for, in a sentence or two.

<AtAGlance menu="Mark ▸ Add Marker" keys="M" tools="add_marker" />

<Shot name="04-editor.window" alt="What the picture shows, for someone who can't see it." />

## Add a marker

<Steps>

1. Move the playhead to the moment.
2. Press <kbd>M</kbd>.

</Steps>

## Options

| Control | What it does | Default |
| ------- | ------------ | ------- |

## Good to know

Limits, edge cases and what stops it, in plain words.

## Related

- [Snapping](/timeline/snapping/)
```

Every section is optional except the opening. Order the task sections as a reader needs them.

- **Headings** start at `##`, are sentence case, and name the job: "Add a marker", not "Adding".
  A feature in `src/data/features.json` with an `anchor` needs a heading that makes that anchor.
- **Menus** are bold with `▸`, spelled as the app spells them: **Clip ▸ Split**.
- **Keys** use the app's symbols in `<kbd>`: <kbd>⌘T</kbd>. Inside `AtAGlance`, pass the string.
- **Controls** are bold where they appear in a step: choose **Save**.
- **Links** are root-absolute with a trailing slash: `/timeline/markers/#add-a-marker`. The build
  fails on a link or anchor that does not exist.
- **Asides** are for what a reader must not miss, not for decoration: `:::note`, `:::tip`,
  `:::caution`, `:::danger`.
- **Screens** come from `src/assets/screens/`. A `name` is the file name without its look and
  extension. Use a screen only when it shows what the page is about, not when the thing is out
  of frame, and give it real alt text.

## MDX traps

MDX is JSX. In prose, `{`, `}` and `<` start code. Put anything like `{x}`, `<1 s` or `a<b` in a
code span, or write it out ("under 1 s"). `<kbd>` and every component must close. A line starting
with `import` or `export` is code. Leave a blank line after an opening component tag and before
its closing tag, or the Markdown inside won't render.

## Checking a page

```sh
node docs/site/scripts/check-pages.mjs <page.mdx>…        # parses, imports, links, captures
python3 tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py --pages <page.mdx>…  # internal words, local paths
pnpm build                                                # in docs/site: the last word
```

## Screens

The captures come from the screen catalog (`designs/screens/`, `tools/proof/screens.py`), so the
pictures are of the real app. To refresh them:

```sh
python3 tools/proof/screens.py --out <dir>                      # from the repository root
node docs/site/scripts/import-screens.mjs <dir> --used
```

**This site is public.** `import-screens.mjs` refuses a capture whose layout dump holds a local
path, and its `CROP` table is the only way past that, by cutting the region away. Settings needs
it: its MCP section prints the helper's full path. Never weaken the refusal.

## When the app changes

A user-visible change edits its page here as well as `docs/guide/`, and a new feature adds its row
to `src/data/features.json`. `tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py` runs in `make test` and fails on a
menu item or agent tool the site doesn't document, a feature whose page or anchor is missing, or a
page that names something internal.

</system-reminder>

---
title: "Type a clip's timing"
description: "Trim a clip to an exact time by typing its In and Out, and read its length, in the Clip tab's Timing section."
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

The Timing section is for when you know the number. Type where a clip starts and ends on the timeline, and read how long it is, without dragging an edge.

<AtAGlance
  where="Clip tab ▸ Clip ▸ Timing"
  tools={['trim_start', 'trim_end']}
/>

## Type In and Out

<Steps>

1. Select one clip.

2. In the [inspector's](/getting-started/inspector/) **Clip** tab, choose the **Clip** sub-tab, the last one. **Timing** is its first section. When the section is shut, its header still shows the clip's length, so click the header to open it.

3. Click **In** or **Out** and type a time. `1:23`, `83.5` and `1:23:04` all work, as they do in the toolbar's time field. See [Inspector fields](/getting-started/inspector-fields/).

4. Press <kbd>Return</kbd>, or click away.

</Steps>

| Field | What it is | What typing does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **In** | Where the clip starts on the timeline | Trims its front edge. The rest of the clip stays where it is. |
| **Out** | Where the clip ends on the timeline | Trims its back edge. |

Both are positions on the timeline, not positions in the file. A later **In** hides the start of the footage, and an earlier one brings it back. To move the whole clip without trimming it, [drag it](/editing/move-clips/) instead.

Each change is one undo step, named Trim Start or Trim End. The time lands on the project's frame grid.

## How far an edge can go

A number out of range doesn't beep. The edge goes as far as it can, and the field shows where it landed.

| Field | Earliest | Latest |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **In** | The start of the timeline, or as far back as the file has footage | One frame before the clip's end |
| **Out** | One frame after the clip's start | As far as the file has footage |

Only a clip that plays a video or audio file has a footage limit. Text, shapes, pictures and graphics have no file length to run out of.

Three things leave the clip as it was:

- If the edge would land where it already is, Frame Job beeps.
- If the text can't be read as a time, Frame Job beeps and the field goes back to the old value.
- If the new edge would break the [overlap rule](/getting-started/refused-edits/), Frame Job beeps and gives the reason at the foot of the inspector.

An overlap the rule allows goes through, and the clip that now overlaps the one before it gets a Cross Dissolve.

## Read the duration

**Duration** shows the clip's length, in the project's [timecode style](/projects/background-and-timecode/). You can't type in it: change the length through **In** and **Out**.

## With several clips selected

**In**, **Out** and **Duration** each describe one clip, so they go away when you select more than one.

If every selected clip plays a video or audio file, Timing stays and holds only the [Reverse](/speed/reverse/) rows, which apply to all of them as one undo step. Its header shows the lengths of the selected clips added together, followed by "total".

If the selection also holds anything else, such as text, a shape, a picture or a freeze frame, there's no Timing section.

## Good to know

- With one clip selected, the Reverse rows appear under **Duration** only for a clip that plays a video or audio file.
- Typing an edge also moves the same edge of a [linked clip](/audio/detach-and-attach/) when the two line up and its track isn't locked. That holds even when you type on the sound half. To move a sound's edge without its picture, [use a drag, <kbd>W</kbd> or <kbd>E</kbd>](/editing/slip-and-roll/#move-a-sound-clips-edge-alone).
- A locked track stops drags, not these fields. If a clip on a locked track is selected, typing still trims it.
- Inside a [nest](/editing/nests/), the times count from the nest's own start.
- [Actions](/motion/how-edits-move-actions/) keep their place measured from the clip's start, so trimming the front edge moves them along the timeline with it.

## Related

- [Trim clips](/editing/trimming/)
- [Slip and roll](/editing/slip-and-roll/)
- [Reverse a clip](/speed/reverse/)
- [Fit a clip to a length](/speed/fit-to-duration/)

---
title: "Slip and roll"
description: "Change which footage a clip shows, or move the cut between two clips, without moving anything else on the timeline."
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Slip and roll are for fine-tuning once your clips are where they belong. A slip changes which part of the file a clip shows. A roll moves the cut between two clips. Neither moves any other clip.

<AtAGlance
  keys={['⌥⇧-drag body', '⌥⇧-drag edge']}
  where="The timeline"
  tools={['slip', 'roll', 'trim_start', 'trim_end']}
/>

## Slip a clip

Hold <kbd>⌥⇧</kbd> and drag the body of a clip. The clip stays where it is at the same length, and the footage slides underneath it. Drag right to show later footage and left to show earlier footage.

The whole drag is one undo step, named Slip. It doesn't change the selection, so you can slip a clip without selecting it.

- A slip stops when the clip reaches either end of its file. If there's no footage to slide into, the drag changes nothing.
- It moves in whole frames and never snaps, because the timeline's snap points mean nothing inside the footage.
- The footage moves at the clip's speed. At ×2, dragging one frame slides the footage two frames.
- A [freeze frame](/speed/freeze-frame/) slips too, which changes the frame it holds. It stops one frame short of the end of its file.
- A linked sound clip on an unlocked track slips with its picture, so the two stay in sync. They move by the smaller of the two distances they each have room for.

Only clips that play a file have footage to slide. The drag does nothing on text, a shape, a picture, a graphic or a nest.

## Roll a cut

Hold <kbd>⌥⇧</kbd> and drag a clip's edge, the outer 7 points of the clip. The cut moves: one clip gets longer and the other gets shorter by the same amount, and the outer edges of the pair stay where they are.

| Edge you drag | Cut that moves |
| --- | --- |
| The clip's start | The cut with the clip before it |
| The clip's end | The cut with the clip after it |

The whole drag is one undo step, named Roll.

- A roll [snaps](/timeline/snapping/) like a trim. Hold <kbd>⌘</kbd> during the drag to stop snapping.
- Each clip keeps at least one frame.
- A clip that plays a file can't grow past what the file has. Text, shapes and pictures have no such limit.
- A roll needs two clips that touch exactly. With a gap at that edge there's no cut to move, and with an overlap there's a [transition](/motion/transition-settings/), whose length you set in its own section. Either way the drag does nothing.
- A clip under about 21 points wide on screen has no edges to grab, and the drag slips it instead. [Zoom in](/timeline/zoom-and-scroll/) first.

When you roll a picture's cut, a linked sound clip rolls with it, as long as it starts at the same point, it touches a clip before it, and its track is unlocked.

## Move a sound clip's edge alone

A [detached sound clip](/audio/detach-and-attach/) that's still linked to its picture can move an edge on its own. This is how a [J-cut or L-cut](/audio/j-and-l-cuts/) is made. These move only the sound's edge and leave the picture where it is:

- Drag the sound clip's edge.
- Select it and press <kbd>W</kbd> or <kbd>E</kbd> to [trim it to the playhead](/editing/trimming/).
- Hold <kbd>⌥⇧</kbd> and drag the sound clip's edge to roll its cut.

It works in that direction only. Trimming or rolling the picture's edge also moves the sound's edge when the two line up, and a slip always takes both.

## What happens to actions and timed words

A slip leaves [actions](/motion/how-edits-move-actions/) where they are, because only the footage inside the clip moves.

A roll leaves each clip's actions at the same distance from that clip's start. So on the clip after the cut, the actions move with the cut along the timeline. On the clip before it, they stay put, and if that clip gets shorter it can end before an action does.

Timed caption words are the exception. They stay on the speech they time, so a roll doesn't shift them against the sound. A [graphic](/graphics/size-and-timing/) after the cut stays in step too: its **In** moves with the cut.

## Good to know

- Neither gesture works on a locked track. The drag does nothing. A linked clip on a locked track stays put while the clip you drag moves.
- On a clip with a [speed ramp](/speed/edit-a-ramped-clip/), the actions stay where they are and the limits come from the ramp, so a cut stops rolling where the clip would no longer fit its file.
- A slip that reaches the end of the footage stops there and keeps what it reached. The drag doesn't turn into a trim.

## With an agent

`roll` can move a picture's cut without its linked sound, which no gesture can. See [Tools: moving and trimming](/mcp/tools-move-and-trim/).

## Related

- [Trim clips](/editing/trimming/)
- [J-cuts and L-cuts](/audio/j-and-l-cuts/)
- [Snapping](/timeline/snapping/)
- [How edits move actions](/motion/how-edits-move-actions/)

---
title: "Split clips"
description: "Cut clips in two at the playhead, and see what each piece keeps of the footage, actions, word timings and graphics."
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Split cuts a clip in two at the playhead, so you can trim, move or remove one piece without touching the other.

<AtAGlance
  menu="Clip ▸ Split"
  keys="⌘T"
  where="The scissors button in the timeline bar"
  tools="split"
/>

## Split at the playhead

<Steps>

1. Move the playhead to the frame you want to cut on.

2. Select the clips to cut, or select nothing to cut everything under the playhead.

3. Press <kbd>⌘T</kbd>.

</Steps>

| What's selected | What gets cut |
| --- | --- |
| One or more clips | Each selected clip the playhead is inside |
| Nothing | Every clip under the playhead on every unlocked track |

It's one undo step, named Split, however many clips it cuts. The command is available whenever the timeline has clips.

The playhead has to be strictly inside a clip. A playhead sitting exactly on a clip's edge is at a cut already, so that clip is left alone. If nothing can be cut, Frame Job beeps and nothing changes.

A clip on a locked track is left alone when nothing is selected, but it's still cut if you selected it.

## Footage stays continuous

The second piece carries on playing the footage from where the first stopped, at the same speed, so the split doesn't show when you play it back. The second piece starts from the values the clip had reached at the cut, and keeps its name, label and settings.

On a clip with a [speed ramp](/speed/edit-a-ramped-clip/), the two pieces meet at exactly the same point in the footage, and the second starts at the rate in force at the cut.

## Linked sound

A [linked clip](/audio/detach-and-attach/) on an unlocked track is cut too, when the playhead is inside it, and the two second halves are linked to each other.

If the linked clip isn't cut, because its track is locked or the playhead isn't inside it, it stays linked to whichever piece shares more of its time. The other piece isn't linked to anything.

## Actions and word timings

[Actions](/motion/how-edits-move-actions/) stay with the piece they fall in:

- An action that ends at or before the cut stays on the first piece.
- An action that starts at or after the cut moves to the second piece.
- An action that spans the cut becomes two. The first half ends at the value it had reached at the cut, and the second carries on to the original target, so the join doesn't show. Both keep the action's curve.

An [entrance and exit preset](/motion/entrances-and-exits/) is tied to the clip's ends, so the first piece keeps the entrance and the second keeps the exit. A [text reveal](/text-and-shapes/text-reveal/) divides the same way. Otherwise the clip would leave at the cut and arrive again on the far side of it.

Caption word timings stay on their words. Both pieces keep the full text, the first with its timings as they were and the second with its timings moved to match its new start.

The one exception is a text clip whose wording an action changes. If the second piece's text at the cut no longer has the same number of words as its timings, the second piece loses its word timings and shows its text all at once.

## Split a graphic

A [graphic](/graphics/size-and-timing/) carries on across the cut rather than starting again, and plays its outro once, at the true end.

The graphic's **In** on the second piece starts at the cut, so it picks up where the first piece left off. Both pieces keep the original's **Length**, so an outro still plays at the same moment. That pins the length, so **Follow Clip** is off on both pieces afterwards.

Trimming the start of a graphic, or [rolling the cut](/editing/slip-and-roll/#roll-a-cut) before it, moves **In** in the same way. Trimming the end leaves a pinned **Length** alone. With **Follow Clip** on, the graphic's own timeline ends at the new end.

## Good to know

- The cut lands on the project's frame grid.
- A [transition](/motion/transitions/) into the clip stays on the first piece. The second piece starts with a hard cut.
- [Sound fades](/audio/fades/) are copied to both pieces. A clip with a fade-in fades in again at the cut, and one with a fade-out dips at the cut, so set them again on the side of the cut where you don't want them.
- A project holds up to 4,096 clips, and a split that would pass that is stopped with a message at the foot of the inspector.

## Related

- [Split at Shot Changes](/editing/split-at-shot-changes/)
- [Delete, Ripple Delete and Lift](/editing/delete-clips/)
- [Trim clips](/editing/trimming/)
- [How edits move actions](/motion/how-edits-move-actions/)

---
title: "Split at Shot Changes"
description: "Cut a finished edit, a download or a stream recording into one clip per shot, with the cuts found on your Mac."
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Split at Shot Changes takes a clip that already has cuts in it, such as a finished edit, a downloaded clip or a stream recording, and cuts it at each one, giving you one clip per shot.

<AtAGlance
  menu="Clip ▸ Split at Shot Changes"
  tools={['split_at_shots', 'get_media_analysis']}
  needs="Nothing. The cuts are found on your Mac, with no key and no upload."
/>

## Split a clip at its shot changes

<Steps>

1. Select one or more clips that show a video file's picture.

2. Choose **Clip ▸ Split at Shot Changes**. It has no shortcut.

3. If Frame Job hasn't looked at this footage yet, wait for the [Analyzing sheet](#while-the-cuts-are-found) to finish.

</Steps>

Each selected clip is cut at every hard cut inside the part of the file it plays. All the cuts are one undo step, named Split at Shot Changes.

The command is greyed out until a selected clip shows a video file's picture. Anything else in the selection is left alone: text, an image, a freeze frame, an audio file, a nest, or a clip with its [picture turned off](/editing/enable-picture-and-sound/).

If the footage holds no shot change inside any selected clip, Frame Job beeps and nothing changes.

## While the cuts are found

When the footage has already been read, the split lands at once. Otherwise the **Analyzing** sheet appears, with one row per file:

| A file's row reads | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| Waiting | Its first frame hasn't been read yet. |
| A percentage, with a bar | How much has been read. |
| Done | Its cuts have been found. |

The split lands as soon as every file is done. Editing commands are off while the sheet is up.

**Stop** closes the sheet and changes nothing. What Frame Job had already found stays in the cache, so it doesn't start from nothing next time.

If the project changes while the sheet is up, nothing is split, and the inspector says to choose the command again.

## What counts as a hard cut

A hard cut is a change from one picture to another between two frames. Frame Job compares each frame's colours with those of the frames before it. It's a plain measurement of the picture, with no machine learning, so the same footage always gives the same cuts.

- A gradual dissolve isn't a cut.
- A single flash frame isn't a cut, because the picture after it matches the one before.
- A dissolve between flat-coloured pictures, such as slides or title cards, can be found as one cut.
- Two shots with very similar colours can be missed, because the comparison looks at colour rather than at what's in the frame.
- Of two cuts within 12 frames of each other in the file, only the stronger is found.

## Found on this Mac and cached

Shot changes are found on your Mac. Nothing is sent anywhere and you don't need a key.

The results are kept in the project's cache, so a second split of the same footage starts at once. See [On-device media analysis](/projects/media-analysis/).

## Where the cuts land

Each cut lands on the project's frame grid, worked out through the clip's speed, [speed ramp](/speed/speed-ramps/) and [reversal](/speed/reverse/). In a project whose frame rate differs from the file's, that's the nearest project frame.

A cut within one frame of either end of a clip isn't made, so you won't get a piece one frame long at a clip's edge.

Each cut is an ordinary [split](/editing/splitting/), so actions, word timings and graphics divide the same way.

## Locked tracks and linked sound

A selected clip on a locked track is still cut. Its linked sound is cut with it when the sound's track is unlocked, as with [Split](/editing/splitting/#linked-sound).

## The clip ceiling

A project holds up to 4,096 clips, counting the clips inside nests. If the splits would pass that, nothing is split at all, and the inspector says how many clips the command would add and how many more would fit. The count includes each linked clip the splits also cut.

## When it can't run

Frame Job beeps and gives the reason at the foot of the inspector:

| What happened | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| A file is missing or can't be read | [Relink it](/projects/relink-media/), then choose the command again. |
| The analysis of a file failed | The message names the file and the reason. Nothing is split. |
| The analysis is no longer in the project's cache | Choose the command again, and Frame Job reads the file again. |

## With an agent

`split_at_shots` works on the clips it's given. Without a list, it takes every clip of a video file on an unlocked track, so a clip on a locked track is cut only when it's named. It shows no sheet. It waits up to 60 seconds for the cuts, and if they aren't ready it stops without splitting and keeps what was found, so calling it again carries on.

`get_media_analysis` reads a file's cuts without splitting anything. See [Tools: cutting and deleting](/mcp/tools-cut-and-delete/).

## Related

- [Split clips](/editing/splitting/)
- [On-device media analysis](/projects/media-analysis/)
- [Select clips](/timeline/selecting-clips/)

---
title: "Delete, Ripple Delete and Lift"
description: "Remove clips or a stretch of the timeline, and choose whether the hole stays open or closes up."
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

There are two delete keys, and the difference between them is what happens to the hole. <kbd>⌫</kbd> leaves it open, so everything else keeps its timing. <kbd>⌘⌫</kbd> closes it, so the rest of the timeline moves left.

<AtAGlance
  menu={['Edit ▸ Delete', 'Edit ▸ Ripple Delete']}
  keys={['⌫', '⌘⌫']}
  where="The Ripple Delete button in the timeline bar"
  tools={['delete', 'ripple_delete', 'lift_range', 'ripple_delete_range', 'ripple_delete_ranges']}
/>

## Choose a delete

Each key acts on the selection, or on the [in/out range](/timeline/in-out-range/) when nothing is selected.

| | Clips selected | Nothing selected, a range set |
| --- | --- | --- |
| <kbd>⌫</kbd> **Edit ▸ Delete** | **Delete:** removes the clips and leaves gaps. | **Lift:** removes what's in the range and moves nothing. |
| <kbd>⌘⌫</kbd> **Edit ▸ Ripple Delete** | **Ripple Delete:** removes the clips and closes each hole. | **Ripple Delete:** removes what's in the range and closes the hole. |

A selection takes priority over a range, so [deselect](/timeline/selecting-clips/) first to act on the range. An empty range is ignored. With nothing to remove, both menu items are greyed out and the keys beep.

## Delete clips and leave a gap

Select the clips and press <kbd>⌫</kbd>. They go, the gaps stay, and nothing else moves. It's one undo step, named Delete.

- A picture takes its [linked sound](/audio/detach-and-attach/) with it, unless the sound's track is locked.
- A linked sound clip goes alone, and leaves its picture silent.
- A clip on a locked track that you selected by clicking is still removed.

## Ripple delete clips

Select the clips and press <kbd>⌘⌫</kbd>, or use the timeline bar's button. The clips go, and each hole closes: everything later on every unlocked track moves left. It's one undo step, named Ripple Delete.

- Each clip's linked partner on an unlocked track goes too, whichever half you selected.
- A clip on a locked track that you selected is removed, but clips on locked tracks don't move.
- [Markers](/timeline/markers/) don't move.

:::caution
Unlike <kbd>⌫</kbd>, <kbd>⌘⌫</kbd> ignores a [selected action](/motion/select-an-action/). With an action selected it ripple-deletes the whole clip. Undo brings it back.
:::

## Lift a range

Set an in/out range, select nothing and press <kbd>⌫</kbd>. Every clip on an unlocked track is cut at both ends of the range, and what lies between is removed. Nothing moves, markers included. It's one undo step, named Lift.

Lift is the safe cut when a mix or a caption track is already timed, because everything after the range keeps its moment. Clips on locked tracks are neither cut nor removed. If the range held nothing to remove, Frame Job beeps.

## Ripple delete a range

Set an in/out range, select nothing and press <kbd>⌘⌫</kbd>. Every clip on an unlocked track is cut at both ends of the range, what lies between is removed, and the hole closes. It's one undo step, named Ripple Delete.

Clips on locked tracks are neither cut, removed nor moved, even inside the range. Everything else after the range moves left by its length, so a locked track falls out of step with the rest. That's what the lock is for.

## How a ripple closes holes

Each hole closes with one shift of everything after it, so clips that touched before still touch.

- A clip past several holes moves by their combined length. Two removed clips that touch leave one hole.
- A clip moves if it starts at or after the end of the hole. A clip on another track that spans the hole stays where it is, and isn't shortened.
- A clip's linked partner on an unlocked track moves with it.
- Markers stay at their times, because a marker inside a removed stretch would have nowhere to go.
- A clip that slides onto a neighbour gets a Cross Dissolve over the overlap. A ripple is never stopped by the [overlap rule](/getting-started/refused-edits/).

One thing does stop a ripple. If it would push a linked clip before the start of the timeline, as a sound leading its picture in a [J-cut](/audio/j-and-l-cuts/) can, nothing moves, and the foot of the inspector names both clips.

## Ripple delete several ranges

An agent can cut a list of time ranges out of the timeline as one edit and one undo step, with `ripple_delete_ranges`. It shows as Ripple Delete under **Edit ▸ Undo**. [Remove Silences](/cleanup/remove-silences/) and [Remove Filler Words](/cleanup/remove-filler-words/) make the same cut from their sheets.

Ranges that touch or overlap merge into one before anything is cut, so two ranges that meet leave one hole, and all the cuts use times from the timeline as it was before the edit. Each range then behaves as [a ripple-deleted range](#ripple-delete-a-range) does: locked tracks are left alone and markers don't move. See [Tools: cutting and deleting](/mcp/tools-cut-and-delete/).

## When the delete keys do something else

<kbd>⌫</kbd> removes the first of these it finds:

1. Words or a pause selected in the [Transcript tab](/captions/delete-words/), while that tab has the focus. They ripple out and the gap closes, as deleting text does.
2. A [selected action](/motion/change-an-action/). The action goes and its clip stays.
3. The selected clips.
4. The in/out range.

<kbd>⌘⌫</kbd> follows the same order without the second step.

While you type in a text field, both menu items are greyed out, so <kbd>⌫</kbd> and <kbd>⌘⌫</kbd> edit the text. That covers the timecode fields, a rename and a text clip.

While a point is selected in a [curve](/color/curves/), <kbd>⌫</kbd> deletes the point and **Edit ▸ Delete** is greyed out.

## Related

- [Close gaps and insert time](/editing/close-gaps/)
- [Split clips](/editing/splitting/)
- [The in/out range](/timeline/in-out-range/)
- [Hide and lock tracks](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/)
- [How a clean-up cut works](/cleanup/how-cleanup-cuts-work/)

---
title: "Close gaps and insert time"
description: "Close an empty stretch of a track with a double-click or Close Gap, and open room on the timeline when you need it."
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Closing a gap pulls everything after it back to meet what's before it, on every unlocked track, so the timeline stays in sync. Opening room does the opposite.

<AtAGlance
  menu="Clip ▸ Close Gap"
  where="Double-click an empty stretch of a lane"
  tools={['close_gap', 'insert_time']}
/>

## Double-click a gap

Double-click an empty stretch of a lane. Everything after the gap, on every unlocked track, moves left by the gap's length. It's one undo step, named Close Gap.

This only works on a lane. Above the first lane or below the last, no track is named, so there's nothing to close.

## Close the gap under the playhead

Move the playhead into a gap and choose **Clip ▸ Close Gap**. It has no shortcut.

It works on the current track: the selected clip's track or, with nothing selected, the front track. The result is the same as a double-click. The command is available when the timeline has clips.

## What moves

- A gap is the empty stretch between two clips on that track. A gap before the first clip closes back to the start of the timeline.
- Every clip on an unlocked track that starts at or after the far side of the gap moves left. A clip on another track that spans that point stays where it is.
- A moved clip's [linked partner](/audio/detach-and-attach/) moves too, when its track is unlocked.
- [Markers](/timeline/markers/) don't move.
- A clip that ends up overlapping the one before it, within the [overlap rule](/getting-started/refused-edits/), gets a Cross Dissolve.

## When a gap won't close

A gap closes completely or not at all. Frame Job beeps, moves nothing and gives the reason at the foot of the inspector when:

| What's wrong | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| The point is on a clip, not in a gap | Move the playhead into the gap, or check the current track. |
| No clip follows the gap on that track | There's nothing to pull back. |
| The track is locked | [Unlock it](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/). Its clips are the ones that would stay behind. |
| Closing it would push clips into an overlap the overlap rule forbids, on any track that moves | Trim or move those clips first. |
| A linked clip would go before the start of the timeline | Happens when a sound leads its picture, as in a [J-cut](/audio/j-and-l-cuts/). Move the pair later, or trim the sound. |

## Insert time

Inserting time opens empty room. Every clip on an unlocked track that starts at or after a point moves later by a length, and so does every marker at or after that point, unlike a ripple.

Clips that span the point stay put, so nothing is cut. To open room inside a clip, [split](/editing/splitting/) it first.

Inserting time has no menu item or gesture of its own. An ⌥-drop [insert](/editing/insert-and-overwrite/) and [Freeze Frame](/speed/freeze-frame/) both do it as part of their edit, and an agent can do it directly with `insert_time`. See [Tools: cutting and deleting](/mcp/tools-cut-and-delete/).

## Open room by hand

<Steps>

1. Move the playhead to where the room should start.

2. Press <kbd>⌥⌘A</kbd> (**Edit ▸ Select After Playhead**) to select every clip that starts at or after the playhead.

3. Drag the selected clips later, or press <kbd>⇧.</kbd> to [nudge](/editing/nudge-clips/) them 10 frames at a time.

</Steps>

This differs from inserting time in two ways: it also moves the selected clips on locked tracks, and it leaves markers where they are. Start the drag on a clip on an unlocked track, because a clip on a locked track can't be grabbed.

## Related

- [Delete, Ripple Delete and Lift](/editing/delete-clips/)
- [Insert and overwrite](/editing/insert-and-overwrite/)
- [Nudge clips](/editing/nudge-clips/)
- [Hide and lock tracks](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/)

# CLAUDE.md — the documentation site

The public user documentation: Astro with Starlight, one page per feature or tight family of
features. `pnpm` manages it, Node is pinned by `.node-version`. `README.md` has the commands.

## Where things are

```
astro.config.mjs        Starlight's settings: title, logo, fonts, theme, plugins
sidebar.mjs             every page's place in the navigation, in order
src/content/docs/       the pages: <section>/<page>.mdx
src/data/features.json  THE FEATURE LIST: what /features/ renders and what the proof reads
src/components/         AtAGlance (a page's facts), Shot (a screen in both looks),
                        FeatureIndex (the filterable list)
src/assets/screens/     WebP captures, written only by scripts/import-screens.mjs
src/styles/             the brand: the mark's inks, the app's faces, square chrome
```

## The rule that matters

**Every claim is written from the code.** A label, a default, a range, a shortcut, a limit or a
refusal is checked against `app/Sources/`, `core/src/`, `graphic/` or `mcp-proxy/` before it is
written, and the code wins over `docs/guide/`, a spec or an ADR. Never write what a feature
probably does. If the code cannot settle it, leave it out.

Nothing dev-only, deferred or unbuilt is documented. That excludes the dev tools (`snapshot_ui`,
`perform_menu_item`, `cancel_sheet`, `select_inspector_tab`, `play_preview`, `graphic_memory`,
`loudness_meter`, `land_recording`, `analysis_job`, `transcript_view`, `playback_rebuilds`,
`assistant_send`, `assistant_answer`) and every `-RCDev` launch default.

## Who reads this

Someone editing a video, who has never read this repository. They want to know what a thing does,
how to do it, and what will stop them. They do not care how it is built.

So a page never mentions: spec or decision IDs (`AU-12`, `§11`), road maps, phases, issue numbers,
source file or type names, `rc_*` exports, format version numbers, proofs, tests, or the history
of a feature. Internal words get translated: "refused" becomes what the user sees ("Frame Job
won't do this while…"), "the core" and "the op" disappear. A tool name is the one exception: the
MCP pages and `tools=` in `AtAGlance` name agent tools, because those are the product's interface.

## Voice

- Plain, direct and second person. Say what it does, then how. Short sentences.
- Open with what the feature is for, in a sentence or two, before any steps.
- British spelling in prose, as `docs/guide/` does (colour, centre, grey, normalise), and the
  app's exact spelling for its own labels (the **Color** tab, **Normalize**).
- Contractions are fine. No marketing: never "powerful", "seamless", "effortless", "robust",
  "simply", "just", "easily", "unleash", "supercharge".
- Prefer a full stop or a comma to an em dash.
- State defaults, ranges and limits as numbers. Say what happens at the edges, because that is
  what a reader comes to a reference for.
- No filler sections. A page with nothing to say under a heading doesn't have that heading.

## Page shape

```mdx
---
title: Markers
description: One sentence, what this page helps you do. Search results show it.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

What the feature is for, in a sentence or two.

<AtAGlance menu="Mark ▸ Add Marker" keys="M" tools="add_marker" />

<Shot name="04-editor.window" alt="What the picture shows, for someone who can't see it." />

## Add a marker

<Steps>

1. Move the playhead to the moment.
2. Press <kbd>M</kbd>.

</Steps>

## Options

| Control | What it does | Default |
| ------- | ------------ | ------- |

## Good to know

Limits, edge cases and what stops it, in plain words.

## Related

- [Snapping](/timeline/snapping/)
```

Every section is optional except the opening. Order the task sections as a reader needs them.

- **Headings** start at `##`, are sentence case, and name the job: "Add a marker", not "Adding".
  A feature in `src/data/features.json` with an `anchor` needs a heading that makes that anchor.
- **Menus** are bold with `▸`, spelled as the app spells them: **Clip ▸ Split**.
- **Keys** use the app's symbols in `<kbd>`: <kbd>⌘T</kbd>. Inside `AtAGlance`, pass the string.
- **Controls** are bold where they appear in a step: choose **Save**.
- **Links** are root-absolute with a trailing slash: `/timeline/markers/#add-a-marker`. The build
  fails on a link or anchor that does not exist.
- **Asides** are for what a reader must not miss, not for decoration: `:::note`, `:::tip`,
  `:::caution`, `:::danger`.
- **Screens** come from `src/assets/screens/`. A `name` is the file name without its look and
  extension. Use a screen only when it shows what the page is about, not when the thing is out
  of frame, and give it real alt text.

## MDX traps

MDX is JSX. In prose, `{`, `}` and `<` start code. Put anything like `{x}`, `<1 s` or `a<b` in a
code span, or write it out ("under 1 s"). `<kbd>` and every component must close. A line starting
with `import` or `export` is code. Leave a blank line after an opening component tag and before
its closing tag, or the Markdown inside won't render.

## Checking a page

```sh
node docs/site/scripts/check-pages.mjs <page.mdx>…        # parses, imports, links, captures
python3 tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py --pages <page.mdx>…  # internal words, local paths
pnpm build                                                # in docs/site: the last word
```

## Screens

The captures come from the screen catalog (`designs/screens/`, `tools/proof/screens.py`), so the
pictures are of the real app. To refresh them:

```sh
python3 tools/proof/screens.py --out <dir>                      # from the repository root
node docs/site/scripts/import-screens.mjs <dir> --used
```

**This site is public.** `import-screens.mjs` refuses a capture whose layout dump holds a local
path, and its `CROP` table is the only way past that, by cutting the region away. Settings needs
it: its MCP section prints the helper's full path. Never weaken the refusal.

## When the app changes

A user-visible change edits its page here as well as `docs/guide/`, and a new feature adds its row
to `src/data/features.json`. `tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py` runs in `make test` and fails on a
menu item or agent tool the site doesn't document, a feature whose page or anchor is missing, or a
page that names something internal.

</system-reminder>
